transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-14 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Sofia (Redwood AE), Rajat (Redwood SE), Maya (NovusEdge CTO), Arjun (Lead ML Eng), Liam (Infra)
---
[00:00] Sofia (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intros, i'm Sofia from Redwood, this is Rajat on the SE side. how are you all doing?
[00:08] Maya (NovusEdge CTO): Good, thanks. Maya here. we've been poking at the hosted API but as we scale to customer-facing features we need capacity predictability and more isolation.
[00:16] Arjun (Lead ML Eng): yep, and we have tight latency SLOs during peak search windows. typical question — reserved GPUs or private onprem?
[00:24] Rajat (Redwood SE): Great, that's exactly what we wanted to unpack. can you run through current qps, model families and peak shaping? even rough numbers help.
[00:33] Liam (Infra): our baseline is ~120 qps for embed endpoints with P95 around 180ms now, spikes up to 1.8k qps for short windows (2-8 mins) during re-ranks. token rates vary a lot; avg request ~60 tokens but some rerank flows hit 300 tokens.
[00:47] Sofia: ok that's helpful. what are your primary constraints? is data residency the blocker for hosted?
[00:52] Maya: residency + customer contractual language on encryption and audit logs. SOC2 is required. also key management — we prefer BYOK with our KMS.
[01:02] Rajat: we support dedicated reserved pools (tenant-isolated) and private deployments (VPC/on-prem) with KMS/HSM integrations. for BYOK we can outline the flow — envelope encryption, audit logs in the console and S3 log export.
[01:14] Arjun: about isolation — we need per-tenant noisy neighbor protection. do you do strict single-tenant nodes or soft fencing?
[01:21] Rajat: reserved pools provide strong tenant fencing; we can present two patterns: dedicated node groups (single-tenant GPUs) or shared warm-pool with strict cgroup/cap enforcement. both have tradeoffs: single-tenant is more expensive but minimal blast radius; warm-pool saves cost and still enforces per-tenant resource quotas and GPU time slicing.
[01:36] Liam: what about prewarm/warm-pool stickiness? our peak bursts are very short and we need to avoid cold-start tail latencies.
[01:42] Rajat: warm-pools can keep KV caches resident and maintain model shards in GPU memory. you can configure stickiness windows (e.g., 5–30 min). we also recommend a small reserved hotpool to handle burst spikes — a mix of reserved and warm pool.
[01:56] Maya: costs — we need rough unit economics. can you send the delta between fully dedicated nodes vs warm-pool hybrid?
[02:03] Sofia: absolutely, we'll send a pricing matrix but quick note: warm-pool hybrid often reduces token cost 20–40% for bursty workloads because of autoscaling and bin-packing. dedicated nodes give predictable throughput and SLOs.
[02:16] Arjun: for the pilot, we want to run with one model variant — 12B dense — and simulate our peak profile. can we run head-to-head with our onprem baseline?
[02:24] Rajat: yes, we usually run a POC with 3 phases — baseline smoke tests, scaled burst simulation, and long-tail failure tests. we can instrument latency, queue depth, and KV cache hit rate. also we'll test quantized variants if you want to trade latency for cost.
[02:38] Liam: curious about eviction and preemption. If other tenants surge, will our reserved nodes be preempted?
[02:44] Rajat: reserved capacity is non-preemptible by design. evictions only happen in soft warm pools with spot-like workers; reserved pools plus SLA mean we won't evict your workloads.
[02:55] Maya: compliance: we need audit trail retention 1 year, SSO with SAML, and key rotation policy docs.
[03:02] Sofia: we have SOC2 Type II and can provide retention and SAML SSO flows. for key rotation we support rotating envelope keys; we'll include the flow in the security pack.
[03:12] Arjun: network topology: traffic will come from our VPC. do you support private link or VPC peering?
[03:17] Rajat: yes, Private has direct VPC peering options and PrivateLink for hosted. for on-prem we support an airgapped deployment too but that adds lead time.
[03:26] Liam: lead time — how long to stand up a dedicated reserved pool?
[03:29] Sofia: for hosted dedicated it's typically 2–4 weeks after contract — depends on region and GPU availability. Private/on-prem is 6–12 weeks largely due to provisioning and network validation.
[03:41] Arjun: for scaling expectations, if our 2-min burst is 15x baseline, will autoscaling handle it or do we need manual warm pool sizing?
[03:49] Rajat: autoscaling is workload-aware but very short, sharp spikes often need a warm pool or prewarmed hotpool to avoid queueing. we'll help model your burst probability and suggest a hybrid sizing (e.g., reserve 20% capacity and configure 100–200 warm slots).
[04:03] Maya: curious about observability — token-level cost, per-route latency, and per-tenant dashboards?
[04:08] Sofia: Redwood Console gives per-route token cost, P95/P99 latency breakdowns, and you can map tokens to customers. we can also add tracing hooks into your existing APM.
[04:18] Arjun: on the POC, we want to validate KV cache benefits. do you instrument cache hit rates?
[04:23] Rajat: yes, we'll surface cache hit rate, average generation time with and without cached prefixes, and cold-start penalty.
[04:30] (crosstalk) Maya: right — and we'll need to ensure model weights never leave our VPC for Private deployment.
[04:35] Rajat: in Private/on-prem model artifacts stay on-customer infra. for hosted dedicated you can also opt for customer-managed keys and strict region pinning.
[04:45] Sofia: ok let me propose an initial POC scope: 2-week benchmark where Redwood stands up a dedicated reserved pool (medium size), we run your 7-day trace replay, we instrument metrics and compare to your onprem baseline. we'll also test a quantized 8-bit variant. does that sound reasonable?
[04:59] Arjun: sounds good. one more question: do you offer contract clauses for performance SLAs?
[05:04] Sofia: yes, Dedicated has SLA tiers; we'll include sample SLA language.
[05:10] Liam: any notable limitations with model types — e.g., attention window, very long context chattiness?
[05:15] Rajat: large contexts are supported; we tune kernels per model. for extremely long context we recommend model sharding and KV-aware eviction tuning. we'll include notes specific to 12B dense.
[05:26] Maya: ok final wrap — we need pricing, security pack, and a POC plan. also, we're evaluating Anthropic for some flows, so include comparison notes if possible.
[05:35] Sofia: noted. we'll include high-level competitor notes and cost delta examples.
[05:40] (brief silence)
[05:44] Sofia: next steps recap: we'll send pricing and security docs; Rajat will send warm-pool/kv cache whitepaper + test harness repo; Arjun will provide traffic traces; we'll schedule a 2-hr POC kickoff next week.
[05:56] Maya: thanks all. excited to see numbers.
[05:59] Sofia: thanks, we'll follow up.
---
